subsystems.name: Sample-prep cartridge
subsystems.role: turns a saliva or blood sample into ready-to-sequence DNA without a lab technician.

subsystems.name: Flow cell and nanopores
subsystems.role: the sensing surface where individual DNA strands are read.
parts: array of hundreds to thousands of wells
motor protein that ratchets DNA through the pore

subsystems.name: Sensor chip
subsystems.role: measures the tiny current changes as each base passes through a pore.

subsystems.name: Onboard compute and software
subsystems.role: turns raw electrical signal into base calls, methylation calls and a report.

subsystems.name: Power, connectivity and app
subsystems.role: makes the device usable outside a laboratory.
parts: wireless link to a phone or laptop

buildSteps.title: Engineer the pore protein
buildSteps.detail: A pore protein is mutated and screened so that each of the four DNA bases blocks the current in a measurably distinct way.

buildSteps.title: Build the flow cell
buildSteps.detail: Pores are inserted into a membrane across an array of microwells, each with its own electrode, on a silicon chip.

buildSteps.title: Design the sensor chip
buildSteps.detail: A custom integrated circuit amplifies currents in the picoamp range and digitises them at kilohertz rates.

buildSteps.title: Simplify sample prep
buildSteps.detail: Reagents and fluidics are packaged so that a swab or finger-prick sample can be processed in a sealed cartridge.

buildSteps.title: Train the basecalling models
buildSteps.detail: Neural networks learn to map characteristic current traces to bases and to methylated bases.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the instrument
buildSteps.detail: Chip, cartridge interface, processor, battery and housing are integrated and calibrated against reference samples.

buildSteps.title: Validate and clear it
buildSteps.detail: The device is tested against clinical-grade sequencing and submitted to regulators for defined health claims.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with surveillance links
buildSteps.detail: Reports feed into public-health systems so that unusual pathogens are flagged early.

prerequisites.why: commercially deployed portable sequencers already read long DNA strands in the field.
methylation can be inferred from the raw current signal without chemical treatment, but accuracy is still improving.
untrained users cannot pipette reagents or run clean-up steps.
basecalling needs substantial compute, which must be cheap and low-power in a home device.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory framework for consumer genetic tests
prerequisites.why: some direct-to-consumer genetic tests are authorised, but broad pathogen and epigenetic claims are not.

pathway.milestone: portable nanopore sequencers used in clinics, field outbreak response and space
pathway.unlocks: proof that sequencing need not live in a central lab.

pathway.milestone: point-of-care cartridges needing no manual library prep
pathway.unlocks: sequencing in small clinics and pharmacies.

pathway.milestone: regulated at-home tests for specific, well-defined conditions
pathway.unlocks: consumer devices with narrow, validated claims rather than open-ended health screening.
early warning of infection and tracking of epigenetic ageing — still largely research.
